jobDescription: A payroll-software company is retiring its legacy job scheduler and moving about 150 internal services to a new orchestration platform over eighteen months. The technical program manager runs the cross-team plan, keeps the RAID log, coordinates readiness reviews with service owners, security and support, publishes weekly status and represents the programme to senior leadership. When migration waves slip or teams disagree on sequencing, the program manager takes the question to the directors with options and is expected to come back with a recorded decision.
requirements: Runs the cross-team programme plan for migrating internal services to the new orchestration platform.
Maintains the programme's risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies (RAID) log.
Coordinates migration readiness reviews with service owners, security and support.
Represents the programme to senior leadership and handles director-level escalations.
Publishes a weekly programme status report.

evidence.text: Technical program manager at Strata Ledger (accounting software), September 2021 to present, running the plan for moving 120 internal services from the legacy job scheduler to the new orchestration platform in six waves.
Kept the programme RAID log, reviewing open risks and dependencies with the service owners every Tuesday and closing items only once the owning team had confirmed them.
Ran readiness reviews for each migration wave with the service owners, the security team and customer support, using a checklist that covered rollback, alerting and support handover.
Calm, inspiring presence in any crisis, with the kind of executive presence that senior stakeholders instinctively trust.

Published the weekly programme status report (waves completed, services blocked, top risks) to the engineering directors' mailing list, with a short section on any wave whose date had moved since the previous week.
Work sample: the readiness checklist used for migration wave 4, completed for 18 services, with the rollback test result, alert ownership and support sign-off recorded for each service.
Reference received from the former director of platform engineering: confirms in writing that the candidate ran the migration programme plan and RAID log from September 2021 to June 2024.
Recruiter logistics note: the candidate has asked for the panel interview to be held in person at the Manchester office and is available to start from 1 December.

propositions.text: The candidate ran the plan for moving 120 internal services from the legacy job scheduler to the new orchestration platform and kept the programme RAID log.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the plan and the RAID log, and the reference check confirms both and the period.

propositions.text: The candidate ran readiness reviews for each migration wave with service owners, security and customer support using a rollback, alerting and support-handover checklist.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the reviews and the work sample shows the completed wave 4 checklist.

propositions.text: The candidate has a strong executive presence that senior stakeholders trust when handling director-level escalations.
propositions.rationale: The entry is the candidate's own description of presence and of how stakeholders feel, with no escalation, option paper or decision behind it. The documented senior-facing work is a weekly status report sent to the directors, so the self-description cannot become a conclusion about handling escalations.

gold.expectedGap: Weekly status reports went to the engineering directors, but no source records the candidate handling a director-level escalation.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the self-description under interview signal risks with its source; keep the plan, RAID log, readiness reviews and status reporting as documented.
followUpTargets: Ask the candidate for an example of a director-level escalation on the programme: what was raised, which options they put forward and what was decided.
